title: Aborting a document load: which tasks to discard?
body:
When [aborting a document load](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#abort-a-document), in Step 2, the spec says to *Cancel any instances of the fetch algorithm in the context of document, **discarding any tasks queued for them**, and discarding any further data received from the network for them.*(emphasis mine).

An 'easy' way to implement this is to cancel all tasks on the networking task source for said document, but that's not what the spec says, and it might be actually too broad in case we expect some of those tasks to still run after abort.

See for example this dicussison: https://github.com/servo/servo/pull/21111#discussion_r204217510

Could we clarify this issue? 

For example, do we expect [pending application cache download process tasks](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#pending-application-cache-download-process-tasks) to still run after the document has been aborted? That's an interesting example because those tasks relate to a fetch that might have already completed before the document gets aborted, hence will not quite fit inside *Cancel any instances of the fetch algorithm in the context of document, discarding any tasks queued for them*.

So I guess the question is, do we want to filter tasks from the networking task source and only cancel those that have a direct relationship with the fetches that we are cancelling as part of document abort? Or could we just clear the entire networking task source for the document? 

**How the EventSource processing model deals with this:**

Note that some tasks, such as 'failing a connection' for an EventSource in response to document abort(see https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#sse-processing-model:fail-the-connection-3), are queued onto another task source, the "remote event" task source in this case, hence are guaranteed to run after the document load has been aborted even if we clear the entire networking task source. 

I think that's a very nice design, and would suggest we update the spec to say that aborting simply clears the networking task source, while moving any tasks we would still expect to run after onto another task source explicitly. 

For example "pending application cache download process tasks" could be queued onto a dedicated "application cache task source", while the actual fetches used by the application cache would still use the networking task source. Aborting a document load would then unambiguously cancel any ongoing fetches related to the application cache, while still run any "pending application cache download process tasks " originating from previously completed loads.
